sanskrit: tasmai prācīnād antardeśād bhavam iṣvāsam anuṣṭhātāram akurvan | bhava enam iṣvāsaḥ prācīnād antardeśād anuṣṭhātā(nu tiṣṭhati ya evaṃ veda) ||
english: For him they made Bhava the archer the attendant from the eastern intermediate region. Bhava, the archer, attends him from the eastern intermediate region — so it is for him who knows thus.

sanskrit: tasmai dakṣiṇāyād antardaśāc charvam iṣvāsam (anuṣṭhātāram akurvan) | śarva enam iṣvāso dakṣiṇād antardeśād (…) ||
english: For him they made Śarva the archer the attendant from the southern intermediate region. Śarva, the archer, attends him from the southern intermediate region — [so it is for him who knows thus].

sanskrit: tasmai pratīcīnād antardeśād rudram iṣvāsam (anuṣṭhātāram akurvan) | rudra enam iṣvāsaḥ pratīcīnād antardeśād (…) ||
english: For him they made Rudra the archer the attendant from the western intermediate region. Rudra, the archer, attends him from the western intermediate region — [so it is for him who knows thus].

sanskrit: tasmā udīcīnād antardeśāt paśupatim iṣvāsam (anuṣṭhātāram akurvan) | paśupatir enam iṣvāsa udīcīnād antardeśād (…) ||
english: For him they made Paśupati the archer the attendant from the northern intermediate region. Paśupati, the archer, attends him from the northern intermediate region — [so it is for him who knows thus].

sanskrit: tasmai dhruvād antardeśād ugraṃ devam iṣvāsam (anuṣṭhātāram akurvan) | ugra enaṃ deva iṣvāso dhruvād antardeśād (…) ||
english: For him they made the fierce god Ugra the archer the attendant from the fixed intermediate region. Ugra the fierce god, the archer, attends him from the fixed intermediate region — [so it is for him who knows thus].

sanskrit: tasmā ūrdhvād antardeśān mahādevam iṣvāsam (anuṣṭhātāram akurvan) | mahādeva enam iṣvāsa ūrdhvād antardeśād anuṣṭhātā (…) ||
english: For him they made Mahādeva the archer the attendant from the upper intermediate region. Mahādeva, the archer, attends him from the upper intermediate region — [so it is for him who knows thus].

sanskrit: tasmai sarvebhyo 'ntardeśebhya īśānam iṣvāsam anuṣṭhātāram akurvan | īśāna enam iṣvāsaḥ sarvebhyo 'ntardeśebhyo 'nuṣṭhātānu tiṣṭhati ya (evaṃ veda) ||
english: For him they made Īśāna the archer the attendant from all the intermediate regions. Īśāna, the archer, attends him from all the intermediate regions — so it is for him who knows thus.

sanskrit: sa dhruvān diśam anu vy acalat | taṃ bhūmiś cāgniś cauṣadhayaś ca vanaspatayaś ca vīrudhaś ca vānaspatyāś cānu vy acalan | bhūmeś ca vai so 'gneś cauṣadhīnāṃ ca vanaspatināṃ ca vīrudhāṃ ca vānaspatyānāṃ ca priyaṃ dhāma bhavati ya (evaṃ veda) | bhūmaye ca vai so 'gnaye cauṣadhibhyaś ca vanaspatibhyaś ca vīrudbhyaś ca vānaspatyebhyaś cā vṛścate ya evaṃ vidvāṃsaṃ vrātyam upavadati ||
english: He moved along the fixed direction. Earth, Fire, the plants, the forest trees, the creeping plants, and the forest growths followed him. He who knows thus comes to the beloved dwelling of Earth, Fire, the plants, the forest trees, the creeping plants, and the forest growths. And he who speaks ill of a vrātya who knows thus cuts himself off from Earth, Fire, the plants, the forest trees, the creeping plants, and the forest growths.

sanskrit: sa ūrdhvāṃ diśam (anu vy acalat) | tam ṛtaṃ ca satyaṃ ca sūryaś ca candramāś cānu vy acalan | ṛtasya ca vai sa satyasya ca sūryasya ca candramāsaś ca (…) | ṛtāya ca vai sa satyāya ca sūryāya ca candramāse ca (…) ||
english: He moved along the upward direction. Ṛta (cosmic order), Truth, the Sun, and the Moon followed him. He who knows thus comes to the beloved dwelling of Ṛta, Truth, the Sun, and the Moon. And he who [speaks ill of a vrātya who knows thus] cuts himself off from Ṛta, Truth, the Sun, and the Moon.

sanskrit: sa bṛhatīṃ diśaṃ (anu vy acalat) | tam ṛcaś ca sāmāni ca yajūṃṣi ca brahma cānu vy acalan | ṛcāṃ ca vai sa sāmnāṃ ca yajuṣāṃ ca brahmaṇaś ca (priyaṃ dhāma …) | ṛgbhyaś ca vai sa sāmabhyaś ca yajurbhyaś ca brahmaṇe ca (…) ||
english: He moved along the vast direction. The Ṛc verses, the Sāmans, the Yajus formulas, and brahman followed him. He who knows thus comes to the beloved dwelling of the Ṛc verses, the Sāmans, the Yajus formulas, and brahman. And he who [speaks ill of a vrātya who knows thus] cuts himself off from the Ṛgveda, the Sāmaveda, the Yajurveda, and brahman.

sanskrit: sa uttamāṃ diśaṃ (anu vy acalat) | tam itihāsaś ca purāṇaṃ ca gāthāś ca nārāśaṃsīścānu vy acalan | itihāsasya ca vai sa purāṇasya ca gāthānāṃ ca nārāśaṃsīnāṃ ca (priyaṃ …) | itihāsāya ca vai sa purāṇāya ca gāthābhyaś ca nārāśaṃsībhyaś ca (…) ||
english: He moved along the highest direction. The itihāsa epics, the purāṇas, the gāthā songs, and the nārāśaṃsī eulogies followed him. He who knows thus comes to the beloved dwelling of the itihāsas, the purāṇas, the gāthās, and the nārāśaṃsīs. And he who [speaks ill of a vrātya who knows thus] cuts himself off from the itihāsas, the purāṇas, the gāthās, and the nārāśaṃsīs.

sanskrit: sa paramāṃ diśam anu vy acalat | tam ṛtavaś cārtavāś ca lokāś ca laukyāś cānu vy acalan | ṛtūnāṃ ca vai sa ārtavānāṃ ca lokānāṃ ca laukyānāṃ ca priyaṃ (dhāma …) | ṛtubhyaś ca vai sa ārtavebhyaś ca lokebhyaś ca laukyaibhyaś cā vṛścate (ya …) ||
english: He moved along the supreme direction. The seasons, seasonal phenomena, the worlds, and the worldly beings followed him. He who knows thus comes to the beloved dwelling of the seasons, the seasonal phenomena, the worlds, and the worldly beings. And he who [speaks ill of a vrātya who knows thus] cuts himself off from the seasons, seasonal phenomena, the worlds, and the worldly beings.

sanskrit: sokadrīcīṃ diśam anu vy acalat tato nāvartsyannamanyata | taṃ virāḍ anu vy acalat sarve ca devāḥ sarvāś ca devatāḥ | virāje ca vai sa sarveṣāṃ devānāṃ sarvāsāṃ ca devatānāṃ ca priyaṃ (…) | virāje ca vai sa sarvebhyaś ca devebhyaḥ sarvābhyaś ca devatābhya ā vṛścate (ya …) ||
english: He moved along the auspicious upward direction, thinking he would not return from there. Virāj followed him, and all the gods and all the divine powers. He who knows thus comes to the beloved dwelling of Virāj, of all the gods, and of all the divine powers. And he who [speaks ill of a vrātya who knows thus] cuts himself off from Virāj, from all the gods, and from all the divine powers.

sanskrit: so 'nādiṣṭāṃ diśam anu vy acalat tato nāvartsyannamanyata | taṃ dakṣiṇāgniś ca gārhapatyaś cāhavanīyaś ca yajñaś ca yajamānaś cānu vy acalan | dakṣiṇāgneś ca vai sa gārhapatyasya cāhavanīyasya yajñasya yajamānasya ca priyaṃ (dhāma …) | dakṣiṇāgnaye ca vai sa gārhapatyāya cāhavanīyāya ca yajñāya ca yajamanāya cā vṛścate (ya …) ||
english: He moved along the unclaimed direction, thinking he would not return from there. The Dakṣiṇāgni fire, the Gārhapatya fire, the Āhavanīya fire, the sacrifice, and the sacrificer followed him. He who knows thus comes to the beloved dwelling of the Dakṣiṇāgni, the Gārhapatya, the Āhavanīya, the sacrifice, and the sacrificer. And he who [speaks ill of a vrātya who knows thus] cuts himself off from the Dakṣiṇāgni, the Gārhapatya, the Āhavanīya, the sacrifice, and the sacrificer.

sanskrit: so 'ntardeśān anu vy acalat | taṃ ditiś caditiś ceḍā cendraṇī cānu vy acalan | diteś ca vai so 'diteś ceḍāyāś cendrāṇyāś ca (priyaṃ …) | ditaye ca vai so 'ditaye ceḍāyai cendrānyai cā (vṛścate …) ||
english: He moved along the intermediate regions. Diti, Aditi, Iḍā, and Indrāṇī followed him. He who knows thus comes to the beloved dwelling of Diti, Aditi, Iḍā, and Indrāṇī. And he who [speaks ill of a vrātya who knows thus] cuts himself off from Diti, Aditi, Iḍā, and Indrāṇī.

sanskrit: sa diśo 'nu vy acalat | taṃ prajāpatiś ca parameṣṭhī ca pitā ca pitāmahaś cānu vy acalan | prajāpateś ca vai sa parameṣṭhinaś ca pituś ca pitāmahasya ca priyaṃ dhāma bhavati ya (evaṃ …) | prajāpataye ca vai sa parameṣṭhine ca pitre ca pitāmahāya cā vṛścate ya evaṃ vidvāṃsaṃ vrātyam upavadati ||
english: He moved along all the directions. Prajāpati, Parameṣṭhin, the father, and the grandfather followed him. He who knows thus comes to the beloved dwelling of Prajāpati, Parameṣṭhin, the father, and the grandfather. And he who speaks ill of a vrātya who knows thus cuts himself off from Prajāpati, Parameṣṭhin, the father, and the grandfather.

sanskrit: sa mahimā sadrur bhūtvāntaṃ bhūmyā agacchat samudro 'bhavat | taṃ prajāpatiś ca parameṣṭhī cāpaś ca śraddhā ca varṣaṃ ca bhūtvānu vy avartanta | taṃ yajñaś ca lokaś cānnaṃ cānnādyaṃ ca bhūtvābhi pary ā vartanta | ainam āpo gacchanty ainaṃ varṣaṃ gacchaty ainaṃ śraddhā gacchaty ainaṃ dīkṣā gacchaty ainaṃ yajño gacchaty ainaṃ loko gacchaty ainam annaṃ gacchaty ainam annādyaṃ gacchati ya (evaṃ veda) ||
english: That greatness, having become a rushing torrent, reached the end of the earth and became the ocean. Prajāpati, Parameṣṭhin, the waters, faith, and rain, taking on those forms, turned back after him. The sacrifice, the world, food, and the enjoyment of food, taking on those forms, turned around him from all sides. Waters go to him, rain goes to him, faith goes to him, consecration goes to him, sacrifice goes to him, the world goes to him, food goes to him, the enjoyment of food goes to him — so it is for him who knows thus.
